<thought>The carbon NMR shows peaks at 135.80, 117.40, 70.50, 54.00, and 43.70 ppm. Typical methyl (CH₃) carbons appear around 10–30 ppm when attached to carbon, but when attached to heteroatoms they shift upfield to ~30–60 ppm (e.g., O‑CH₃ ~55 ppm, N‑CH₃ ~40 ppm). Here we have two peaks in that hetero‑atom region (54.00 ppm and 43.70 ppm), suggesting two distinct CH₃ groups. No peaks are in the aliphatic methyl region (10–30 ppm), so there are no simple alkyl methyls. Therefore, the molecule likely contains two methyl groups overall.</thought>
<final_answer>2</final_answer>
